newsitem.title: USA: NYS gov says balancing budget hinges on Medicaid.
newsitem.headline: NYS gov says balancing budget hinges on Medicaid.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki, who on Tuesday unveiled an ambitious $66 billion budget for fiscal 1998 that contains big tax cuts but raises school spending, admitted it hinges on slashing Medicaid costs.
Asked if it would be difficult to balance to budget without Medicaid cuts, the Republican governor told reporters at a news conference here: "Yes."
Pataki's plan calls for slashing Medicaid spending by $572 million to $25.4 billion, two percent less than the current year.

Such a huge reduction can be achieved because the state is shifting more of the people who get Medicaid to managed care and because hospitals profits rose strongly last year, he explained, estimating the rise in earnings at around $400 million.

However, the governor did not hesitate to make it clear that his budget faces signficant roadblocks in negotiations with the Assembly, which is led by Democrats, and with the Senate, which is controlled by Republicans.

Asked whether it was likely that the legislature might seek to raise spending rather than inflict spending cuts, he replied: "I think the likelihood of that is 100 percent. If history is any guide, it's extremely unlikely that the legislature is going to come in and say you're spending too much."

Pataki, whose budget last year set a national record for tardiness, added that he did not plan to push for a constitutional amendment to allow casino gambling, at least in the short-term. "It's not on my agenda over the course of month to be looking at a constitutional amendment."
Saying he would not twist lawmakers' arms to approve the measure, he noted it is one he favors. "I support the amendment. I would like to see it pass."
